chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he brought out to us the ring of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and the ring of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). And it was inscribed on the ring of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'You are my trusted one, so protect me from the people.' And the engraving of the ring of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was: 'Allah is sufficient for me,' and in it was a rose and a crescent in its upper part.

key_terms.خَاتَم: Ring (used as a seal or ornament)

ai.seo_question: What are the inscriptions on the rings of the Imams mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the physical legacy of the Imams, specifically the rings of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Imam Musa al-Kadhim, as preserved by Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr. The inscriptions 'You are my trusted one, so protect me from the people' and 'Allah is sufficient for me' reflect key Shia theological concepts of divine protection and sufficiency, while the accompanying rose and crescent motifs illustrate the aesthetic and symbolic traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. This narration serves as a primary source for understanding the authenticity and design of the Imams' personal seals.
